verdict: Confirmed normal-pressure guard aborts during streamed target weight loading, not target inference. No measured causal attribution to a loader leak; active MLX follows trusted loaded-prefix bytes. A bounded Python payload lifetime inefficiency is reproduced and an allocation-reducing candidate is CPU-tested only.

812 target tensors / 7425163456bytes on rank0 and1042 /9137972032bytes on rank1 match trusted headers for frozen28/36. At abort, active MLX exceeds completed serialized prefix by only263338..313106bytes, not another multi-GB copy.

Confirmed Python-level lifetime defect: tensor_records keeps the previous payload while allocating the next; send_records also keeps its prior record during next(). This is bounded overlap, not an accumulating full-checkpoint retention leak.

actual_loading_trace.finding: Process-local recommended wired limit is set before generation. Strict group init and reporting precede small_gate. Small mlx_lm.load defaults lazy=False. Hidden gate creates a small head;025 additionally pipeline-shards the small model and runs overlap gates. small_gate returns receipt dictionaries, not its model. Local module/output/small_head bindings survive del model and the in-function gc/clear_cache until the helper returns; their late destruction can refill the allocator cache.

Upstream loader collects mx.load arrays into a weights dict, constructs Model, calls sanitize, quantizes modules, assigns all weights, and evaluates only final model.parameters when lazy=False. Sanitization makes Python dicts that reuse array objects; canonical conv [dim,kernel,1] and norms are not numerically transformed. Raw-HF conv layouts can create moveaxis/+1 lazy arrays, but target streamed canonical tensors bypass sanitizer entirely. Small model weights dict is local to load_model and is not returned; tokenizer and model references end with small_gate. No full27B upstream loader is reached in these trials.

Remote CPU server reads headers only for admission, selects rank0 tensors, then per sorted name opens a file, seeks, reads one payload, closes file before yield, hashes, and sends it. Local receiver validates config/rank/split, allocates one exact-sized bytearray with recv_into, yields a record, and assigns it through load_from_tensors. No target shard is mmap-loaded; there is no mx.load call in server or stream_weights. Hashlib digests do not create a full tensor copy.

Rank1 opens the same remote checkpoint via local-file stream records in its own process, not mlx_lm.load. Metadata maps cover all headers but contain no weight bytes. Each tensor read can populate OS file cache independently of Python heap lifetime. Concurrent CPU server reads rank0 payloads on this same host; remote file-cache/process overlap is therefore plausible but not measured.

Model creates full64-layer random FP32 lazy graph plus replicated embedding and head; eval() switches training mode, not mx.eval. pipeline removes nonowned layer references before nn.quantize. Quantize traverses/replaces retained leaf modules; from_linear/from_embedding temporarily instantiate another quantized module then replace its random graph with quantization of the original random float weight. These are source-level lazy graph lifetimes, not demonstrated allocated full-precision tensors. Before first target record, observed active memory is only4654/5966bytes, directly inconsistent with an eagerly allocated52.8/65.0GB retained constructor or full target copy.

expected holds initial parameter array references only through metadata validation and is deleted before loading. Python loop variable initial is not deleted and retains the last initial array until function exit; it can prolong an unevaluated random quantization graph. No operation in the loop evaluates initial. Its actual graph/storage size is not measured, and it cannot be treated as a measured multi-GB resident duplicate.

np.frombuffer(...).reshape is a view over the Python payload; mx.array(view) creates the runtime array, BF16 uses a dtype view, mx.eval(array) completes that tensor, and load_weights(list,strict=False) directly replaces the named array rather than opening files or sanitizing. Loader deletes consumer references and clears free allocator cache after every tensor. Full model.parameters is evaluated only after exact complete loaded-name coverage. The C++ iterator array initializer allocates/copies, but the installed Python numpy binding implementation was not available; exact numpy-binding ownership and staging-copy count were not executed or asserted. Budget a current tensor CPU source plus runtime destination; do not assert persistent two-model duplication.

mapping_and_copy_limits.target_file_handle_lifetime: tensor_records with-block closes before yield; checkpoint_inventory header/base reads use short with-blocks.
mapping_and_copy_limits.small_mx_load: Reached once before target. Installed Load primitive owns shared_ptr<io::Reader>; ParallelFileReader opens FD in constructor and closes in destructor. Deferred load readers may survive until lazy load graphs are evaluated/released.
mapping_and_copy_limits.mmap_claim_limit: The compiled loader/Python binding .cpp implementations were not found locally. These declarations are not proof that mx.load uses mmap, or that every underlying read buffer/mapping releases at a particular point. No such mapping was measured. In any event this cannot introduce a full27B mx.load mapping in a target path that never calls mx.load.
mapping_and_copy_limits.interpretation: Post-small free cache is a concrete short-lived overhead; the first tensor_done clear_cache removes it. It is not the cache reported at the pressure-abort boundary. Any OS file cache, compression, physical footprint, paging or retired Metal allocations is distinct and unmeasured here.

ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.hypothesis: Normal accumulated target weights plus host-wide resource state cross the pressure1 boundary; not a new025 multi-GB MLX weight leak.
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.support: Active MLX matches the exact trusted completed prefix within <314KB on both trials. Cache is0 at abort. Same loader bytes previously completed both full shards. Different abort tensor positions with pressure2 are compatible with different host headroom/residency, not a fixed tensor corruption.
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.not_proven: No per-host available/resident/wired/compressed/file-cache ledger was captured alongside these loading events; host background state, actual residency, wired-limit policy and file-cache contribution cannot be separated. OS pressure is global, MLX active is not RSS, and maxRSS is a high-water process statistic.
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.prediction: A complete ledger would place most active allocation in unique completed parameters and show no persistent second target copy; missing capacity would be explained by other resident/wired/compressed/cache consumers.
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.smallest_next_diagnostic: Use this CPU prefix-ledger analysis and existing baseline receipts first. Only the parent hardware owner may later passively sample host-wide memory around already-authorized work; this audit requests no launch or full-model retry.
